analysis.title: Inside Commodities, November 20, 2026
key_insights: US shale producers (Devon, ConocoPhillips, Diamondback, Occidental, APA, EOG) returned about $7.25B via dividends and buybacks in Q3, up 41% y/y and about $2.11B more than a year earlier. Brent is up more than 50% in 2026 on Middle East supply disruptions.

Exxon held shareholder returns at $9.4B and Chevron at nearly $6B in Q3. Rystad's Matthew Bernstein says the supermajors directed oil-price windfall cash to debt reduction. Exxon plans to hold buybacks at $20B in 2027.

Shale producers guide to restrained 2027 output: Diamondback, EOG, ConocoPhillips and Devon forecast low single-digit production growth, Occidental flat, APA similar US and Egypt volumes. Diamondback's Q3 reinvestment rate was 32% vs 36%-37% a year earlier.

Melius' James West says oil in the mid-$80s would historically have lifted E&P budgets within a quarter or two, but shale spent roughly what was budgeted at the start of the year. He says output could rise if the Middle East conflict ends and oil stays above $80.
Brent has ranged from $59.75 to $126.41 in nine months and is currently above $90, per the Diamondback CEO and GL Consulting commentary.

The US naval blockade of Iranian oil since July has removed more than 1M bpd of discounted crude from Chinese teapot refiners. Iranian oil was 13.6% of China's 2025 imports (Kpler). Replacement crude carries premiums of $6-$20 per barrel over Brent, vs Iranian discounts of $10-$11 earlier in the year.

Shandong teapot utilisation was 54.7% in the week ended Nov 12, up from sub-50% in Q2 but well below the 65%-75% of 2020-2021. Energy Aspects expects a floor near 50% through year-end. Analysts do not expect widespread closures.

China's oil imports for Jan-Oct were 399.9M tons (9.6M bpd), down 15.1% y/y. Refiners are buying on demand rather than stockpiling, which caps China's purchases. November teapot margins are losing an estimated 150-200 yuan per ton ($3-$4 per barrel).

Crude flows out of the Strait of Hormuz have largely returned to pre-war levels despite Iranian attacks on tankers, but prices remain elevated. Iraqi Basrah premiums fell to about $6 over Brent from $10-$13 as freight retreated from records. Russian ESPO is about $22 over Brent.

Brazil's corn ethanol now exceeds a quarter of ethanol output. DDG/S feed output rose from 280,000 tons to over 4.8M tons in 2025-26 and is expected at 5.71M in 2026-27. Feedlot cattle hit 9.25M head in 2025 (22% of slaughter) and are forecast at 9.78M this year.

Corn ethanol breakeven in Mato Grosso was 1.84 reais per liter in July vs 2.22-2.36 for center-south sugarcane ethanol (USDA). Co-products are about 25% of plant revenue. Brazil has 29 corn ethanol plants operating and 27 under construction or planned.

India's wheat planting was 5M hectares by Nov 13, down 15.3% y/y. The 2026/27 area is expected to fall about 6% from last year's record 33.6M hectares to 31.58M, the steepest drop since 2000/01. Monsoon rain was as much as 41% below average in key states and El Niño adds yield risk. The minimum support price rose only 1%.

China's refined copper imports for Jan-Oct fell 16% y/y to 2.37M tons, the lowest for the period since at least 2015. A Reuters poll of 15 analysts expects imports to rise in 2027 on tight concentrate supply. CRU sees China copper demand up 4% in 2027 after 2% this year. Argus expects only a moderate recovery.

The US has proposed a 15% tariff on refined copper imports from 2027, with implementation unclear. Argus notes Section 232 authority survives the midterms. Codelco is offering lower 2027 premiums to Chinese buyers.

Lynas Rare Earths faces its AGM on November 25 without a permanent CEO after a favored candidate withdrew. Shares are down 42% from the April 15-year high and trade near 10-year-low forward EV/EBITDA. Takeover vulnerability is flagged. Pol Le Roux has been interim CEO since June.

The EU agreed Thursday to delay its methane regulation for importers by a further 12 months. The Center for LNG says US exporters, with about 160 mtpa of export capacity, are now more comfortable signing long-term European contracts. The US signed deals with Montenegro, Albania, Hungary's 4iG and Poland's Orlen, and is finalising a deal to supply 20% of Czech LNG consumption.

The US Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act 62-33. It speeds permitting for power plants, transmission lines and data centers and requires large AI data centers to cover more grid upgrade costs. It now goes to the House, and Trump has said he will sign it.
Indonesia plans tighter soybean import controls (permits, inspection, essential-goods status) proposed from January 1. About 85% of its 2025 soybean imports came from the US ($1.03B of $1.19B).

China's October soybean imports fell 23% y/y to 7.3M tons. Brazil shipments were 6.6M tons (-7% y/y, -38% m/m) and US shipments 0.18M tons (-56% m/m). Jan-Oct US imports are down 33% y/y to 11.3M tons. China has bought over 60% of its 25M-ton US target for 2026/27.

market_movers.rationale: Expects buybacks to exceed $1B this quarter and rise further in 2027, with low single-digit production growth.
Buybacks to rise in Q4, targets returning 45% of operating cash flow in 2027, dividend raised 11%.
Raised dividend 7%, reinvestment rate fell to 32% from 36%-37%.
Raised dividend 8% and guides to low single-digit 2027 production growth.
Plans another $650M of buybacks by year-end and at least 60% of annual free cash flow returned.
Prioritizes shareholder returns with flat 2027 production.
Held Q3 returns at $9.4B and plans $20B of 2027 buybacks, with excess cash going to debt reduction.
Held Q3 shareholder returns at nearly $6B, with windfall cash going to debt reduction.
Cited only as precedent: it bought Newcrest in 2023 while Newcrest had no permanent CEO, relevant to Lynas takeover talk.

sector_views.rationale: Windfall cash is going to dividends and buybacks with restrained production growth, supporting returns.
Chinese import recovery is expected in 2027, but US tariff uncertainty and a weak 2026 base cap conviction.
India's acreage drop and El Niño yield risk threaten supply and favor higher prices.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 reported results: Devon, ConocoPhillips, Diamondback, Occidental, APA and EOG returned about $7.25B via dividends and buybacks, per Reuters calculation. This is reported data, not an estimate.
Q3 2026 reported: Diamondback reinvestment rate 32% vs 36%-37% a year earlier. Dividend increases: Diamondback +7%, EOG +8%, ConocoPhillips +11%.
Q3 2026 reported: Exxon returns $9.4B and Chevron nearly $6B, both unchanged. Exxon guides to $20B of 2027 buybacks (company guidance).
Company guidance: ConocoPhillips aims to return 45% of 2027 cash flow from operations. APA targets at least 60% of annual free cash flow. Devon expects buybacks above $1B in Q4.

macro_indicators.reading: above $90/bbl; 2026 range $59.75-$126.41; up more than 50% in 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: Elevated prices persist despite Hormuz flows returning near pre-war levels, supporting shale cash returns and raising costs for Chinese refiners.
Weaker Chinese demand for crude as teapots lose Iranian barrels and buy on demand.
Lowest for the period since at least 2015, leaving room for a 2027 rebound.
Brazil and US arrivals both fell m/m, reducing near-term import pull.
Early sowing is well behind, consistent with the expected 6% full-season decline.
Average of 10 industry officials. It would be the steepest fall since 2000/01.
CRU projection that supports higher refined imports.
Above Q2's sub-50% lows but far under 65%-75% in 2020-2021. Energy Aspects sees a floor near 50% through year-end.
Up from 4.8M tons in 2025-26, supporting feedlot growth.

risk_factors: Peace in the Middle East with oil staying above $80 could lead shale producers to raise output, per Melius.
Teapot margin losses of $3-$4 per barrel and weak Chinese fuel demand risk deeper run cuts.
US tariff on refined copper (15% from 2027) may not be implemented, leaving flows uncertain.
El Niño and weak monsoon threaten India's wheat yields and acreage.
Lynas's CEO search may extend past the Nov 25 AGM, leaving it exposed to a takeover.
The EU methane regulation could be extended to a third year, per Riedl, since it is unclear whether a trigger exists.
vol_and_positioning: Brent has traded between $59.75 and $126.41 in nine months, an extreme range that Diamondback's CEO describes as 'all over the place'.
geopolitical: US naval blockade of Iranian oil shipments since July, removing more than 1M bpd from Chinese teapot refiners.
Iran war and Middle East conflict supporting high oil prices, with Iranian attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz.
EU delay of methane regulation tied to energy market disruption from the Iran war.
US-China soybean trade: China bought about 12M tons of US soybeans after an October summit, and has bought over 60% of its 25M-ton target.
Indonesia negotiating a reciprocal trade agreement with the US while tightening soybean import controls.
Proposed US 15% tariff on refined copper imports from 2027 and Section 232 authority after the midterms.
US-EU energy cooperation: LNG deals signed at the P-TEC conference in Warsaw.

tension_points.bull_case: Producers are keeping reinvestment low and returning cash, which supports dividends and buybacks (Diamondback, ConocoPhillips, APA).
tension_points.bear_case: Melius says output could rise if the Middle East conflict ends and oil stays above $80, which would pressure prices and end the capital discipline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Middle East conflict ending with oil holding above $80 a barrel.

tension_points.bull_case: 15 analysts expect imports to climb in 2027 on tight concentrate supply and demand growth of 4% (CRU).
tension_points.bear_case: Argus expects only moderate normalisation and only if the US arbitrage stays less attractive. A 15% US tariff could redirect flows.
tension_points.what_invalidates: US implementation of the proposed 15% refined copper tariff from 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Corn ethanol DDG/S supply is a clear facilitator and is pulling new producers into feedlots (ASSOCON, IMEA).
tension_points.bear_case: DSM-Firmenich's Walter Patrizi sees broader structural agricultural advances as the primary driver, not ethanol.

theme_stances.key_argument: Independents adjust buybacks to cash flow and are raising returns while holding production growth low.
theme_stances.evidence: The independents tend to adjust their buyback activity based on their current cash flows

theme_stances.key_argument: China will have to import more refined copper next year because its refined production growth will remain very limited.
theme_stances.evidence: China will have to import more refined copper next year

theme_stances.key_argument: Weak monsoon and low water availability push farmers away from wheat toward chickpeas and rapeseed.
theme_stances.evidence: India's wheat acreage is poised for its steepest decline in 26 years
